Polysomnography Report

Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnography.
Clinical Indication: Excessive daytime sleepiness, reported snoring, and witnessed apneas.

This was a technically adequate overnight diagnostic polysomnogram. Total sleep time was 345
minutes with a sleep efficiency of 82%. Sleep architecture was abnormal due to significant sleep
fragmentation. REM sleep was reduced, comprising only 10% of total sleep time.

Frequent respiratory events were noted throughout the night. The overall Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI)
was 42 events per hour, which is in the severe range. These events were predominantly obstructive
apneas and hypopneas, and they were more severe during REM sleep. This was associated with
significant oxygen desaturation, with a nadir SpO2 of 78%. The patient's baseline oxygen saturation
was 95%. No significant periodic limb movements were noted.

The findings are consistent with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).

A follow-up appointment is recommended to discuss treatment options, including positive airway
pressure (PAP) therapy. A subsequent PAP titration study under polysomnography is indicated to
determine the optimal pressure for treatment.

Clinical History: 29-year-old female with a known history of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE),
presenting with new-onset proteinuria and hematuria. Biopsy is performed to evaluate for lupus
nephritis.

Diagnosis: Kidney, native, biopsy: Lupus Nephritis, Class IV-G (A)

Light Microscopy Description: The specimen consists of two cores of renal cortex and medulla. Up to
28 glomeruli are identified for evaluation. All glomeruli show global, diffuse endocapillary and
mesangial hypercellularity with neutrophilic infiltration. Multiple glomeruli contain wire loop lesions.
There is moderate tubular atrophy and interst ial fibrosis involving approximately 30% of the cortex. No
crescents or fibrinoid necrosis are seen.

Immunofluorescence Description:

IgG: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops (full house pattern).
IgA: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.

IgM: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.

C3: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.

C1q: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.

Fibrinogen: Negative.

Albumin: Negative.

Electron Microscopy Description: Electron microscopy confirms diffuse subendothelial and
mesangial electron-dense deposits. Tubuloreticular inclusions are present within endothelial cells.
There is approximately 50% podocyte foot process effacement.

Comment: The combined findings are diagnostic of active, diffuse global lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS
2003 Class IV-G (A). ; ;
